title: An optimized protocol for combined fluorescent lectin/immunohistochemistry to characterize tissue-specific glycan distribution in human or rodent tissues
protocol: Leave tissue frozen sections on a slide warmer at room temperature for 30 minutes to 1 hour before starting the staining.
Incubate sections with 4% PFA solution on the slide for 2 minutes if tissue was not fixed prior to freezing.
Circle each tissue section with a PAP pen to create a hydrophobic barrier and prevent leakage of lectin solution.
Wash sections with TBS-T three times for 3 min each at room temperature in a glass Coplin staining jar on a shaking platform.
Lay out the slides horizontally with tissue sections facing up in an opaque StainTray slide staining system.
Block sections with 3% periodate-treated BSA in TBS for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash sections with TBS three times for 3 min each at room temperature in a glass Coplin staining jar, shaking gently.
Incubate sections with fluorescently labeled lectins diluted in TBS-T for 1 hour at room temperature (~18°C–23°C) in a dark chamber.
Prepare fresh working solutions of lectins 30 minutes before each staining and discard them at the end of the experiment.
Pre-incubate each lectin with 100 mM of the appropriate sugar in TBS-T at RT (~18°C–23°C).
Incubate lectins prepared in the relevant sugar in TBS-T for at least 30 min before adding to tissue.
Continue sugar-lectin co-incubation on the tissue.
Perform a positive control using a tissue section known to display glycan residues specific to the lectin.
Wash sections with TBS-T twice, for 3 min each.
Wash sections once with TBS without detergent at room temperature (approximately 18°C–23°C).
Wash brain tissue twice with TBS-T for 10 minutes each.
Wash brain tissue twice with TBS for 10 minutes each.
Counterstain with Hoechst 33342 diluted 1:2,000 in TBS for 5 to 10 minutes at room temperature.
Wash sections with TBS three times for 3 minutes each at room temperature.
Incubate brain tissue with 0.1% Sudan black B solution in 70% ethanol for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Wash brain tissue twice with TBS for 4 minutes each at room temperature.
Wash excess Hoechst 33342 from tissue sections.
Apply one or two drops of Fluoromount™ aqueous mounting media and cover the slide with a glass coverslip.
Leave slides to cure overnight (~16 h) at RT (~18°C–23°C, in the dark).
Seal around the edges of the coverslip with clear nail polish.
Store slides at 4°C until imaging.
Image stained slides by using a fluorescence microscope.
Acquire images from several planes within the tissue section for confocal microscopy.
Critical: Image stained slides within 4 days.
Carry out immunohistochemistry after lectin staining.
Place tissue sections in a humidified chamber covered with TBS if continuation is delayed.
Conduct all immunostaining steps in darkness or red-light room.
Maintain slides in a humidified chamber to prevent drying during immunostaining.
Perform a prior optimization for the immunostaining.
Determine the optimal primary antibody dilution.
Incubate the primary antibody overnight at 4°C or for 2 hours at room temperature.
Test both TBS and TBS-T to find the solution that avoids interference with an optimal positive signal intensity.
Conduct negative control experiments by incubating sections with a non-related or isotype control antibody.
Assess non-specific binding of the secondary antibody to the tissue in negative controls.
Block with normal serum if necessary, but be aware it may affect previous lectin binding.
Employ appropriate controls during staining optimization to ensure accurate results.
Carry out all immunostaining steps using TBS and do not switch to PBS.
Keep slides in the StainTray slide staining system and block with 3% periodate-treated BSA in TBS.
Incubate sections with primary antibody at the concentration, time and temperature optimized previously.
Wash sections twice with TBS-T for 10 min each.
Wash sections once with TBS for 10 min.
Incubate sections with fluorescently labeled secondary antibody diluted in TBS.
Prepare fresh working solutions for injection 30 minutes before each time point.
Wash sections with TBS three times, for 3 min each at room temperature (approximately 18°C–23°C).
If staining brain/cardiac tissue or other tissues rich in auto-fluorescent lipofuscin, wash once with TBS-T for 10 minutes and then three times with TBS for 10 minutes.
Counterstain sections either with Hoechst 33342 diluted 1:2,000 (final concentration at 0.01 mM) in TBS for 5 to 10 min at room temperature or with ProLong Gold Antifade Mountant with DAPI.
If Hoechst 33342 is used as the counterstain, wash sections with TBS three times, for 3 min each.
Incubate brain tissue or other tissues rich in auto-fluorescent lipofuscin with 0.1% Sudan black B solution in 70% ethanol for 5 minutes at room temperature after washes.
Wash tissue twice with TBS, each for 4 minutes at room temperature.
Apply one or two drops of Fluoromount™ aqueous mounting media and cover slide with a glass coverslip.
Leave slides to cure overnight (~16 h) at room temperature in the dark.
Seal around the edges of the coverslip with clear nail polish to prevent the coverslip from sliding and the mountant from drying out.
Store stained slides at 4°C until imaging or store at -20°C for up to one month if necessary.
Image stained slides using a fluorescence microscope.
